title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Set Definition and Representation
text:
Set Definition and Representation

Key terms: set, element, roster form, set-builder form

A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects, called elements. Sets can be represented in roster or tabular form (listing elements) or set-builder form (describing elements with a common property).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Set Definition and Representation in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Set Membership and Symbols
text:
Set Membership and Symbols

Key terms: ∈, ∉

Elements belong to a set (denoted by '∈') and can be represented using the Greek symbol '∈' (epsilon) or '∉' (not an element of).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Set Membership and Symbols in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Empty Set

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Empty Set in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Finite and Infinite Sets
text:
Finite and Infinite Sets

Key terms: finite set, infinite set

A finite set has a definite number of elements, while an infinite set has an infinite number of elements. Infinite sets can be represented using three dots (e.g., {1, 2, 3, ...}).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Finite and Infinite Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Equal Sets
text:
Equal Sets

Key terms: equal sets, repeated elements

Two sets are equal if they have exactly the same elements. Sets do not change if elements are repeated.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Equal Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Set Equality
text:
Set Equality

Key terms: set, element, equal

Two sets are equal if they contain the same elements, regardless of the order or repetition. Elements of a set are unique.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Set Equality in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Null Set
text:
Null Set

Key terms: null set, empty set, ∅

A null set, or empty set, is a set that contains no elements. It is denoted by the symbol ∅.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Null Set in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Subset
text:
Subset

Key terms: subset, ⊆, ⊄

A set A is a subset of set B (denoted A ⊆ B) if every element of A is also an element of B. If A is not a subset of B, we write A ⊄ B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Subset in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Proper Subset
text:
Proper Subset

Key terms: proper subset, ⊂

A set A is a proper subset of set B (denoted A ⊂ B) if A is a subset of B and A ≠ B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Proper Subset in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Union of Sets
text:
Union of Sets

Key terms: union, ∪

The union of sets A and B (denoted A ∪ B) is the set of all elements that are in A, in B, or in both.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Union of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Intersection of Sets
text:
Intersection of Sets

Key terms: intersection, ∩

The intersection of sets A and B (denoted A ∩ B) is the set of all elements that are in both A and B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Intersection of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Universal Set
text:
Universal Set

Key terms: universal set, U

The universal set (denoted U) is the set that contains all the elements being considered in a particular context.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Universal Set in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Venn Diagrams
text:
Venn Diagrams

Key terms: Venn diagram

Venn diagrams are used to represent sets and their relationships. They consist of rectangles and closed curves, usually circles, to represent sets and their subsets.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Venn Diagrams in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Intersection of Sets
text:
Intersection of Sets

Key terms: intersection, ∩

The intersection of two sets is the set of elements that belong to both sets. It's represented as A ∩ B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Intersection of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Union of Sets
text:
Union of Sets

Key terms: union, ∪

The union of two sets is the set of elements that belong to either set. It's represented as A ∪ B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Union of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Difference of Sets
text:
Difference of Sets

Key terms: difference, -

The difference of two sets A and B (A - B) is the set of elements that belong to A but not to B.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Difference of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Complement of a Set
text:
Complement of a Set

Key terms: complement, A'

The complement of a set A with respect to the universal set U (A') is the set of elements in U that are not in A.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Complement of a Set in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | De Morgan's Laws
text:
De Morgan's Laws

Key terms: De Morgan's laws

De Morgan's laws state that (A ∪ B)' = A' ∩ B' and (A ∩ B)' = A' ∪ B'.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to De Morgan's Laws in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Russell's Paradox
text:
Russell's Paradox

Key terms: paradox, set theory, self-membership

A paradox in set theory, showing that not all sets can be members of themselves, leading to inconsistencies.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Russell's Paradox in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Zermelo's Axiomatization
text:
Zermelo's Axiomatization

Key terms: axiomatization, Zermelo, set theory

The first formal system of axioms for set theory, published in 1908 by Ernst Zermelo to address paradoxes.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Zermelo's Axiomatization in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Fraenkel's Axiom
text:
Fraenkel's Axiom

Key terms: Fraenkel, axiom, set theory

An additional axiom proposed by Abraham Fraenkel in 1922 to further address paradoxes in set theory.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fraenkel's Axiom in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Von Neumann's Axiom of Regularity
text:
Von Neumann's Axiom of Regularity

Key terms: Von Neumann, axiom, regularity

Introduced by John Von Neumann in 1925, this axiom states that every set is either empty or contains an element that is not a member of the set itself.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Von Neumann's Axiom of Regularity in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Bernays' Axiomatization
text:
Bernays' Axiomatization

Key terms: Bernays, axiomatization, set theory

A set of axioms for set theory proposed by Paul Bernays in 1937, providing a more satisfactory foundation for the subject.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Bernays' Axiomatization in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Gödel-Bernays Set Theory
text:
Gödel-Bernays Set Theory

Key terms: Gödel, Bernays, set theory, consistency

A modification of Bernays' axiomatization by Kurt Gödel, also known as Von Neumann-Bernays set theory, which is a consistent and widely accepted foundation for modern mathematics.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Gödel-Bernays Set Theory in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Cantor's Set Theory in Modern Mathematics
text:
Cantor's Set Theory in Modern Mathematics

Key terms: Cantor, set theory, modern mathematics

Despite the paradoxes, Cantor's set theory is widely used in present-day mathematics, with most concepts and results being expressed in the set-theoretic language.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Cantor's Set Theory in Modern Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cantor's Set Theory in Modern Mathematics in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Cartesian Product of Sets
text:
Cartesian Product of Sets

Key terms: Cartesian product, ordered pair

The Cartesian product of two sets A and B, denoted A × B, is a set of all ordered pairs (a, b) where a is an element of A and b is an element of B. The order of elements in the pair matters.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Cartesian Product of Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Relation between Sets
text:
Relation between Sets

Key terms: relation, domain, range, codomain

A relation R from a set A to a set B is a subset of the Cartesian product A × B, where each ordered pair (a, b) in R satisfies a specific condition relating a and b.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Relation between Sets in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Function - Special Relation
text:
Function - Special Relation

Key terms: function, domain, range, image, preimage

A function is a special type of relation where every element in the domain has exactly one image in the range. It's a rule that assigns to each element of the domain exactly one element of the range.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Function - Special Relation in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Real Valued Function
text:
Real Valued Function

Key terms: real valued function, real function

A real valued function is a function where both the domain and the range are subsets of real numbers. It's a function that maps real numbers to real numbers.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Real Valued Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Real-valued Function
text:
Real-valued Function

Key terms: domain, range, real numbers

A real-valued function is a relation where both the domain and range are subsets of real numbers. If the domain is all real numbers, it's called a real function.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Real-valued Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Identity Function
text:
Identity Function

Key terms: identity, domain, range

The identity function is a real-valued function where the output is equal to the input for every element in its domain.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Identity Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Constant Function
text:
Constant Function

Key terms: constant, domain, range

A constant function is a real-valued function where every element in its domain maps to the same output.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Constant Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Polynomial Function
text:
Polynomial Function

Key terms: polynomial, variable, power

A polynomial function is a real-valued function that can be expressed as a polynomial equation, where the output is a sum of terms consisting of variables raised to non-negative integer powers.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Polynomial Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Quadratic Function
text:
Quadratic Function

Key terms: quadratic, coefficient, variable

A quadratic function is a real-valued function where the output is a quadratic equation, i.e., an equation of the form ax² + bx + c, where a ≠ 0.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Quadratic Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Rational Function
text:
Rational Function

Key terms: rational, polynomial, denominator

A rational function is a real-valued function where the output is a ratio of two polynomials, with the denominator not equal to zero.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Rational Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Modulus Function
text:
Modulus Function

Key terms: modulus, absolute value

The modulus function is a real-valued function that takes the absolute value of its input, i.e., it returns the non-negative value of the input.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Modulus Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Signum Function
text:
Signum Function

Key terms: signum, positive, negative

The signum function is a real-valued function that returns 1 if the input is positive, 0 if the input is zero, and -1 if the input is negative.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Signum Function in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Trigonometry Origin and Applications
text:
Trigonometry Origin and Applications

Key terms: trigonometry, applications, triangles

Trigonometry was originally developed to solve geometric problems involving triangles. It has wide-ranging applications in fields like navigation, surveying, engineering, seismology, electric circuits, atomic physics, oceanography, music, and more.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Trigonometry Origin and Applications in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Angle Measurement Units
text:
Angle Measurement Units

Key terms: angle, degrees, radians, revolutions

Angles can be measured in degrees, radians, or revolutions. One revolution is equivalent to 2π radians or 360 degrees.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Angle Measurement Units in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Radian Measure
text:
Radian Measure

Key terms: radian, measure, circle, arc, radius

Radian measure is the unit of angle in which one radian is defined as the angle subtended at the center of a circle by an arc that is equal in length to the radius of the circle.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Radian Measure in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Degree to Radian Conversion
text:
Degree to Radian Conversion

Key terms: degrees, radians, conversion, π, 180

To convert degrees to radians, multiply by π/180. To convert radians to degrees, multiply by 180/π.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Degree to Radian Conversion in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Trigonometric Functions Definition
text:
Trigonometric Functions Definition

Key terms: trigonometric, functions, unit circle, radian, definition

Trigonometric functions like sine, cosine, tangent, etc., are defined using a unit circle with the origin as the center. They are extended to any angle in terms of radian measure.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Trigonometric Functions Definition in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Behavior of Cosecant Function in Fourth Quadrant
text:
Behavior of Cosecant Function in Fourth Quadrant

Key terms: cosecant, fourth quadrant, arbitrarily large

The cosecant function decreases from -1 to -∞ in the fourth quadrant, and assumes arbitrarily large negative values as x approaches 2π.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Behavior of Cosecant Function in Fourth Quadrant
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Behavior of Cosecant Function in Fourth Quadrant in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Values of Trigonometric Functions for Special Angles
text:
Values of Trigonometric Functions for Special Angles

Key terms: special angles, unit circle, trigonometric functions

The values of sine, cosine, and other trigonometric functions for special angles like 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90° can be found using the unit circle or special triangles.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Values of Trigonometric Functions for Special Angles
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Values of Trigonometric Functions for Special Angles in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles
text:
Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles

Key terms: sum and difference, unit circle, sine and cosine addition formulas

Formulas for sine, cosine, and other trigonometric functions of the sum and difference of two angles can be derived using the unit circle or the sine and cosine addition formulas.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Double Angle Formulas for Sine and Cosine
text:
Double Angle Formulas for Sine and Cosine

Key terms: double angle, unit circle, sine and cosine addition formulas

The double angle formulas for sine and cosine, such as sin(2x) = 2sin(x)cos(x) and cos(2x) = cos^2(x) - sin^2(x), can be derived using the unit circle or the sine and cosine addition formulas.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Double Angle Formulas for Sine and Cosine
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Double Angle Formulas for Sine and Cosine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Sum and Difference Identities for Sine and Cosine
text:
Sum and Difference Identities for Sine and Cosine

Key terms: sum and difference, unit circle, sine and cosine addition formulas

The sum and difference identities for sine and cosine, such as sin(x + y) = sin(x)cos(y) + cos(x)sin(y) and cos(x + y) = cos(x)cos(y) - sin(x)sin(y), can be derived using the unit circle or the sine and cosine addition formulas.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Sum and Difference Identities for Sine and Cosine
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Sum and Difference Identities for Sine and Cosine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Double Angle Formula for Sine
text:
Double Angle Formula for Sine

Key terms: sin, cos, 2x

sin(2x) can be calculated using the identity sin(2x) = 2sin(x)cos(x).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Double Angle Formula for Sine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Double Angle Formula for Cosine
text:
Double Angle Formula for Cosine

Key terms: cos, sin, 2x

cos(2x) can be calculated using the identity cos(2x) = cos^2(x) - sin^2(x) or 2cos^2(x) - 1.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Double Angle Formula for Cosine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Sum-to-Product Identities
text:
Sum-to-Product Identities

Key terms: sin, cos, x, y

sin(x+y) and cos(x+y) can be calculated using sum-to-product identities like sin(x+y) = sin(x)cos(y) + cos(x)sin(y).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Sum-to-Product Identities in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Difference-to-Sum Identities
text:
Difference-to-Sum Identities

Key terms: sin, cos, x, y

sin(x-y) and cos(x-y) can be calculated using difference-to-sum identities like sin(x-y) = sin(x)cos(y) - cos(x)sin(y).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Difference-to-Sum Identities in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Co-function Identities
text:
Co-function Identities

Key terms: sin, cos, π/2, x

sin(π/2 - x) = cos(x) and cos(π/2 - x) = sin(x) are examples of co-function identities.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Co-function Identities in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Even-Odd Identities
text:
Even-Odd Identities

Key terms: sin, cos, x

sin(-x) = -sin(x) and cos(-x) = cos(x) are examples of even-odd identities.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Even-Odd Identities in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Induction Formula for Sine
text:
Induction Formula for Sine

Key terms: sin, n, x

sin(nx) can be calculated using the induction formula sin(nx) = sin[(n-1)x]cos(x) + cos[(n-1)x]sin(x).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Induction Formula for Sine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Induction Formula for Cosine
text:
Induction Formula for Cosine

Key terms: cos, n, x

cos(nx) can be calculated using the induction formula cos(nx) = cos[(n-1)x]cos(x) - sin[(n-1)x]sin(x).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Induction Formula for Cosine in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Complex Numbers
text:
Complex Numbers

Key terms: complex number, real part, imaginary part

A number of the form a + ib, where a and b are real numbers, is called a complex number. The real part is 'a' and the imaginary part is 'b'.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Complex Numbers in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Addition of Complex Numbers
text:
Addition of Complex Numbers

Key terms: addition, complex numbers

The sum of two complex numbers z1 = a + ib and z2 = c + id is (a + c) + i (b + d).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Addition of Complex Numbers in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Multiplication of Complex Numbers
text:
Multiplication of Complex Numbers

Key terms: multiplication, complex numbers

The product of two complex numbers z1 = a + ib and z2 = c + id is (ac - bd) + i (ad + bc).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Multiplication of Complex Numbers in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Multiplicative Inverse of a Complex Number
text:
Multiplicative Inverse of a Complex Number

Key terms: multiplicative inverse, complex number

For any non-zero complex number z = a + ib (a ≠ 0, b ≠ 0), the multiplicative inverse is given by 1/z = a - ib / (a^2 + b^2).

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.topic: Multiplicative Inverse of a Complex Number
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Multiplicative Inverse of a Complex Number in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Power of i
text:
Power of i

Key terms: power, i

For any integer k, i^4k = 1, i^4k + 1 = i, i^4k + 2 = -1, i^4k + 3 = -i.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Power of i in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Conjugate of a Complex Number
text:
Conjugate of a Complex Number

Key terms: conjugate, complex number

The conjugate of a complex number z = a + ib is z* = a - ib.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Conjugate of a Complex Number in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Complex Number Equality
text:
Complex Number Equality

Key terms: complex number, real part, imaginary part

Two complex numbers are equal if their real and imaginary parts are equal.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Complex Number Equality in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Power of i
text:
Power of i

Key terms: i, power, periodicity

For any integer k, i^4k = 1, i^4k + 1 = i, i^4k + 2 = -1, i^4k + 3 = -i.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Power of i in Grade 11 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 11 Mathematics | Conjugate of a Complex Number
text:
Conjugate of a Complex Number

Key terms: conjugate, complex number, real part, imaginary part

The conjugate of a complex number z = a + ib is z* = a - ib.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Conjugate of a Complex Number in Grade 11 Mathematics.

text:
Historical Recognition of Imaginary Numbers

The Greeks recognized that square roots of negative numbers do not exist in the real number system, but Indian mathematicians Mahavira and Bhaskara were the first to clearly state this difficulty.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Historical Recognition of Imaginary Numbers in Grade 11 Mathematics.

text:
Acceptance of Imaginary Numbers

Key terms: imaginary numbers, square roots, i

Albert Girard was the first to accept square roots of negative numbers, and Euler introduced the symbol i for the square root of -1.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Acceptance of Imaginary Numbers in Grade 11 Mathematics.

text:
Definition of Complex Numbers by Hamilton

William Rowan Hamilton defined complex numbers as ordered pairs of real numbers, avoiding the use of 'imaginary numbers'.

metadata.topic: Definition of Complex Numbers by Hamilton
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Definition of Complex Numbers by Hamilton in Grade 11 Mathematics.

Graphical Representation of Inequalities

text:
Systems of Inequalities

Solving multiple inequalities simultaneously, finding the intersection of their solution sets, and representing the solution region on a number line or coordinate plane.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Systems of Inequalities in Grade 11 Mathematics.

text:
Inequalities in Real-life Applications

Key terms: real-life application, modeling, temperature, mixture

Using inequalities to model and solve real-world problems, such as finding the range of temperatures or mixture concentrations.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Inequalities in Real-life Applications in Grade 11 Mathematics.

text:
Solving Linear Inequalities

Find values of x that make an inequality true. Use inverse operations to isolate x.

text:
Graphing Inequalities on Number Line
